https://statehouse.gov.sc/news/7270/pres.text: News President Herminie and Czech President Pavel Discuss Strengthening Seychelles–Czech Cooperation 23 September 2026 | ⤢ President Dr Patrick Herminie held bilateral talks with President of the Czech Republic H.E. Petr Pavel on the margins of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The meeting provided an opportunity for the two leaders to discuss avenues for strengthening cooperation between Seychelles and the Czech Republic, with particular attention to areas where Czech expertise and technology could support Seychelles’ development priorities. President Pavel highlighted the potential for Czech companies to explore opportunities in Seychelles in sectors including agriculture, transport, smart city solutions and water management. He noted that Czech businesses have experience in providing tailored solutions in different countries and expressed the view that cooperation could be based on partnerships, technology transfer and the involvement of small and medium-sized enterprises. He emphasised that the role of government is to help open opportunities for businesses from both countries to connect and identify areas where they can work together, while ensuring that cooperation responds to the specific needs of each country. The two Presidents also discussed opportunities for greater cooperation in training and education. President Pavel described education as an important bridge between countries and highlighted the longstanding links created through students from different African countries who studied in the former Czechoslovakia and the Czech Republic. President Dr Patrick Herminie took the opportunity to express Seychelles’ interest in deepening cooperation between the University of Seychelles and Czech universities, including Charles University, through academic exchanges, joint research and short-term placements. He noted that areas of mutual interest could include medicine, environmental science, aquatic ecosystems, biodiversity and climate resilience. The discussion also touched on areas of specialised training, including the Czech Republic’s experience in training service dogs, with the possibility of exploring opportunities for exchanges and cooperation in this field. On international cooperation, President Pavel underlined the Czech Republic’s support for strong international institutions and a rules-based international system, including the role of the United Nations in providing a framework for cooperation among countries. He also informed President Herminie of the Czech Republic’s intention to present its candidacy for a non-permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council for the 2032–2033 term and expressed his country’s interest in Seychelles’ support. The talks also provided an opportunity to reflect on the historical links between the Czech Republic and Seychelles, including the presence of Seychellois and Czech nationals who have contributed to exchanges between the two countries over the years. Both sides expressed the view that there is scope to further develop relations between Seychelles and the Czech Republic, particularly through business partnerships, education, training and the exchange of expertise. President Herminie was accompanied at the meeting by members of the Seychelles delegation attending the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly. Share this article

Photograph: Thierry Monasse/Getty Images Ukraine Trump’s pause on Russia sanctions is ‘reward’ for Putin, Zelenskyy says Ukrainian president warns it will embolden Russian leader and intensify war as Moscow hits country’s power plants Power plant attacks reflect Russian blueprint to make Ukrainian cities unlivable Andrew Roth in Kyiv Sat 17 Oct 2026 10.46 EDT First published on Sat 17 Oct 2026 09.28 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Volodymyr Zelenskyy has described Donald Trump’s decision to roll back sanctions on Russia as a “reward” for Vladimir Putin and warned it will embolden the Russian leader and intensify the Kremlin’s war, as Moscow launched one of its worst strikes yet on Ukraine’s power plants in an attempt to black out the country’s cities before winter. The Ukrainian president also said he expected the Trump administration to lift more sanctions against Russia in the future and called for Europe to establish its own negotiations with Moscow as the US has sought better ties and business deals with the Kremlin. “Unfortunately, the lifting of sanctions will continue, and I believe that the ‘diesel deal’ is the first step,” said Zelenskyy on Saturday. “Unfortunately, it seems to me that this cannot stop Putin; on the contrary, he feels joy and happiness that he has such support.” In a social media message earlier, Zelenskyy wrote: “A US ⁠sanctions blackout, easing pressure on the aggressor, financial rewards for Putin – all of this only encourages him to keep attacking. We must not give up ground. “We must keep trying to end the ‌war. To end it, not give Putin every reason to continue it indefinitely.” View image in fullscreen A policeman helps an elderly woman to walk out from a residential building damaged by a Russian airstrike in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine. Photograph: Kateryna Klochko/AP In its latest effort to reduce tensions with Russia , Trump announced on Friday that he would put a hold on a sweeping new sanctions package targeting the Russian economy, telling Congress the pause on the legislation passed by both chambers was in the national interest. The act, named for the late senator Lindsey Graham, who championed the legislation , would have introduced tough new sanctions on Russia including a 100% tariff on major importers of Russian oil such as China and India, as well as sanctions on Russia’s energy sector, financial institutions and shadow fleet of oil tankers. On Saturday, Zelenskyy said the decision to waive the sanctions would encourage Vladimir Putin to intensify the war in Ukraine and called for support in the US to resurrect the bill. “At the time when the Russians launched such a massive strike against our energy sector, in America, regrettably, a decision was made to completely ignore the Lindsey Graham law, which was supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to end this war,” he wrote in a statement. “This law could have – and still can! – help a great deal. But the law needs to actually work, and every voice in support of it matters.” View image in fullscreen A car burns after a Russian airstrike on a residential neighborhood in Zaporizhzhia. Photograph: Kateryna Klochko/AP The move was greeted by the Russian presidential envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, who wrote on social media: “The Trump administration’s suspension of the Graham Act is an important and truly historic moment.” The legislation, which sanctions Russian officials, banks and a shadow fleet of tankers that keeps the country’s energy supplies moving, was due to be implemented in two days. It also directs Trump to impose up to 100% tariffs on the top five importers of Russian oil or natural gas, with an exception for countries that import less than 15% of Russia’s natural gas exports and have taken significant steps to reduce those imports. Friday’s announcement comes a week after Trump said the US had agreed to purchase diesel from Russia to try to bring down global energy prices, upending years of US and western pressure on the Kremlin to end its war against Ukraine. Trump said last week that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tonnes in November and 1m tonnes “immediately thereafter”. Russia would deliver an additional 3m tonnes “within a short period of time” after that, he wrote. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines Europe A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day after newsletter promotion View image in fullscreen A protest calling for the resignation of Kyiv mayor Vitaly Klitschko, amid anger over increasing cost of public transport, the destruction of Kyiv’s green spaces and handing them over for development, and insufficient funding for the Ukrainian army from the city budget. Photograph: Sergey Dolzhenko/EPA The Trump administration’s decision to waive the sanctions is the latest consequence of a brutal quarrel between Trump and Zelenskyy. Several times this week, the US did not provide intelligence of impending ballistic missile attacks to Ukraine , and the White House reportedly ordered the Pentagon to throttle the military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet network used by Ukraine’s armed forces to run its drone operations on the frontline. “We very much hope – and I personally hope – that the president of the United States of America will do everything so that Putin stops the killings, stops the strikes on our energy infrastructure, and stops this war,” Zelenskyy said on Saturday. “But once again, you cannot achieve this by restricting Ukraine’s responses to Russia for killing our people. And even less so by lifting sanctions.” Trump has demanded that Ukraine halt its strikes on Russian oil refineries, as he has blamed the war in Ukraine, rather than the closure of the strait of Hormuz, for the worldwide spike in diesel prices. Ukraine unilaterally halted the strikes after Trump declared an “energy ceasefire” last week, but resumed them when it became clear that Russia was stepping up its attacks on Ukrainian power plants and substations. View image in fullscreen A mobile blast shelter installed in Kyiv for emergency protection during air raid alerts. Photograph: Danylo Antoniuk/Anadolu/Getty Images Zelenskyy said on Saturday that Russia had launched one of its worst strikes yet against the country’s energy infrastructure, hitting more than 15 critical power generation and transmission facilities and causing “severe consequences”. He also indicated that Ukraine’s dwindling stock of anti-air weapons made it difficult to shoot down many of the loitering munitions, cruise missiles and ballistic missiles being launched each night at Ukraine. “Although our warriors are shooting down a significant number of them,” he said, the “sheer scale and unrelenting pace of Russia’s strikes, specifically against our energy sector, are unfortunately having severe consequences.” Explore more on these topics Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy Donald Trump Russia Vladimir Putin US foreign policy Europe news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story Power plant attacks reflect Russian blueprint to make Ukrainian cities unlivable Trump calls Ukraine’s renewed strikes on Russian oil refineries ‘a disgrace’ Russia and Ukraine trade strikes as Trump ‘energy ceasefire’ collapses Volodymyr Zelenskyy feels ‘betrayed’ by Donald Trump over Starlink access Ukrainian military’s access to Starlink satellite internet suddenly restricted Did Ukrainian strikes on Russian datacentres reduce online disinformation? https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachric.text: Network X 2026 Brings Europe's Telecom Leaders Together in Vienna to Define the Future of Connectivity A1 Group, Swisscom, Orange, Deutsche Telekom, Vodafone, Drei Austria, 4iG, Kyivstar and other industry leaders headline telecoms premier event Network X 2026 unites the telecommunications industry's most influential executives and technology leaders at VIECON Vienna from 13-15 October, with a high-powered Headliners programme focused on the forces reshaping the future of connectivity. Across three days, CEOs, CTOs, technology chiefs, regulators and industry experts from leading operators and technology organisations will examine how artificial intelligence, network sovereignty, broadband networks, 6G, cloud, infrastructure investment and new business models are changing the role of the telecom operator. The programme features senior executives from A1 Group, Swisscom, Drei Austria, A1 Austria, Orange, Deutsche Telekom, Vodafone Group, Kyivstar, 4iG Telecommunications Holding, Yettel Bulgaria, Play Poland, Orange Slovensko, NGMN Alliance and other major players across the global connectivity ecosystem. Industry Leaders Take the Stage Network X 2026 will feature a series of keynote presentations, fireside conversations and high-level executive panels exploring the industry's most pressing strategic questions. Headline speakers include: Christoph Aeschlimann, Group CEO, Swisscom Aeschlimann will join senior industry leaders for "Sovereignty, AI Factories the Future of European Telecoms" to examine Europe's growing focus on digital sovereignty, AI infrastructure and strategic control of critical technology. Volodymyr Lutchenko, COO, Kyivstar With "From Resilience to Competitive Advantage," Lutchenko will explore how resilience, infrastructure and technological agility can become strategic advantages for operators navigating increasingly complex environments. Laurent Leboucher, Group CTO and EVP Networks, Orange - Leboucher will join global technology leaders for "Shaping the 6G Era From Vision to Sustainable Network Evolution" to examine the evolution from 5G towards sustainable, intelligent and commercially viable 6G networks. Volker Libovsky, CTIO, Magenta Austria Examining the transformation of communications networks, "From Connecting People to Connecting Our (Intelligent) World" sees Libovsky outline how intelligence becomes increasingly embedded across connected environments. Dr. Takki Yu, Vice President and Head of Infra Tech Office, SK Telecom Dr. Yu will showcase how AI is moving from experimentation into practical network operations with his "AI in Action: Transforming Network Operations at SK Telecom" keynote session. Melinda Szabo, CEO, T-Mobile Czech Republic Slovak Telekom Szabo will lead a fireside chat entitled "Scaling AI in Telco: Driving Scale While Maintaining Local Relevance" to discuss the challenges and opportunities of scaling AI across telecom organisations while maintaining market-specific relevance. Rudolf Schrefl, CEO, Drei Austria Hosting a keynote panel, "Investment, Regulation Value Creation in Austria's AI-Driven Telecom Future," Schrefl will join senior Austrian technology and regulatory leaders to examine investment, regulation and value creation as AI transforms the sector. Christian Laque, CTO, A1 Austria During "Redefining the Future of Networks," Laque will contribute to an executive discussion on how network architectures and operator strategies are evolving in response to AI and emerging technologies. Mariusz Gatza, CEO, Orange Slovensko Gatza's "AI at the Top: The Leadership Decisions Defining the Next Decade" session will explore the leadership decisions operators must make as AI moves from experimentation towards large-scale deployment. Tamás Tábori, Chairman and CEO, 4iG Telecommunications Holding Tábori will join senior industry executives for "The Great Telco Rebuild: M&A, Capital and Control in the AI Infrastructure Era," a panel addressing how AI-driven demand, shifting ownership models and private investment are reshaping the future of telecom infrastructure. Jan Oetjen, CEO, FRITZ! Oetjen's keynote presentation, "Full Control Over Hardware, Software and Data: Sovereignty in Practice" will spotlight what digital sovereignty means in practice and why control over hardware, software and data is becoming increasingly important. "The next era of the telecoms industry is being built now," said Chris Lycett, Event Director, Network X. "AI is changing the network, data centres are shifting priorities, fixed and mobile continue to converge and sovereignty is changing the infrastructure equation. Network X brings these conversations together under one roof, putting attendees in the room with the people deciding what happens next." Network X Awards Highlights This year's Network X Awards continue to unite leading telecoms innovators on 14 October at Vienna's Museum of Applied Arts (MAK). Recognising the companies and operators pushing the boundaries of network infrastructure, AI, fibre, optical transport and next-generation connectivity, this year's shortlist spans 21 categories with leading technology providers and telecom operators competing for recognition across some of the industry's most critical areas of innovation. The following have been shortlisted for the awards: Bitdefender have been shortlisted in the Most Innovative Smart Home Experience Award for their Smart Home Security and Home Network Protection product with Swisscom. TP-Link have been shortlisted in two categories this year: the Best AI Security on Home Router category and the Best Indoor Connectivity Solution category. Airties have been shortlisted in the Leading In-Home Wi-Fi Service for their Data-Driven, Proactive Wi-Fi Optimization Program with Vodafone. Smartone Solutions have been shortlisted in the Best Smart Home Customer Experience Award for their Cullinan Harbour Transformation. With its combination of C-suite leadership, operator case studies, strategic debate and deep technical expertise, Network X provides a forum for the telecommunications industry to examine not simply what comes next, but how operators can turn emerging technologies and infrastructure investment into sustainable competitive advantage. Data Center World Europe will take place alongside Network X on 13-14 October 2026 at VIECON, providing a platform for leading data centre executives to address the challenges and opportunities of powering the data centres of tomorrow. Registered Network X conference attendees will enjoy full access to Data Center World Europe. For more information on the programme and to register for a pass, visit www.networkxevent.com. About Network X Network X will debut in Vienna on 13-15 October 2026 as the only global event uniting the fixed and mobile telecommunications industries under one roof. Bringing together more than 5,500 senior network infrastructure and service professionals including 1,500+ operators the event convenes telecom leaders, technology vendors, policymakers, analysts and media from across the global communications ecosystem. The event is recognised as a critical meeting point for operators and vendors shaping the future of digital infrastructure, enabling attendees to exchange ideas, build strategic partnerships and explore next-generation technologies transforming communications worldwide. With a focus on advancements in connectivity, AI-driven transformation, and the journey towards full fibre and 6G, Network X provides a comprehensive platform for professionals to learn, engage, and network with experts, technology providers, and peers across the telecommunications landscape. For more information, visit www.networkxevent.com.
